View `single c j` as a functor and use its canonical identifications at degree `j`:
\[
X(\operatorname{single} A)_j \simeq A,\qquad
\operatorname{cycles}(\operatorname{single} A)_j \simeq A,\qquad
\operatorname{opcycles}(\operatorname{single} A)_j \simeq A.
\]

The main mechanism is naturality and coherence of these three isomorphisms.

Organize the argument around two small goals:

1. Show that the quotient/projection map
   \[
   X(\operatorname{single} A)_j\to\operatorname{opcycles}(\operatorname{single} A)_j
   \]
   becomes the canonical map \(X(\operatorname{single} A)_j\to A\) after composing with the inverse opcycles identification. This gives the first conjunct.

2. For \(f:A\to B\), express the degree-\(j\) component of `single.map f` by transporting \(f\) across the canonical `X` isomorphisms. The cycles-map equation is the same naturality statement transported through the canonical cycles isomorphisms. Thus both sides of the `Iff` are equivalent formulations of naturality of the supported-degree identification.

After unfolding only the relevant canonical isomorphisms and functor maps, the remaining work should be standard category simplification using associativity and the hom–inverse cancellation identities. The essential assumptions are the zero object and zero morphisms, which make the unsupported differentials vanish and hence produce the cycles/opcycles identifications.
